expectations.text: Cites the information supplement Security Considerations for AI Systems published in September 2026
expectations.evidence: Never names 'Security Considerations for AI Systems' or September 2026; refers only to 2025 assessor guidance and vague 'AI principles... (2025 and after)' with a caveat 'not of every title and date'.

expectations.text: Explains information supplements are guidance and do not create new requirements
expectations.evidence: 'has published AI-related material, though there is no AI-specific requirement in PCI DSS itself' — material is guidance, not new requirements.

expectations.text: Notes Secure SLC v2.0 (September 28, 2026) also addresses AI and digital tools in lifecycle processes
expectations.evidence: No mention of the Secure SLC Standard or its v2.0 release anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: Confirms PCI DSS v4.0.1 itself is unchanged by the supplement
expectations.evidence: Never cites the supplement nor mentions v4.0.1, so it cannot and does not confirm v4.0.1 is unchanged by it; only the generic 'no AI-specific requirement in PCI DSS itself'.

expectations.text: Gives practical application advice for AI touching cardholder data environments
expectations.evidence: Nine-point program covering scope, keeping PAN out of prompts/training data, access control for AI agents, Req 12.8 for AI vendors, logging, testing and an AI use policy.
